n: A fountain will be opened to cleanse David’s house and Jerusalem from sin and impurity. Christians see this fountain in the cleansing power of Christ’s Atonement.
God will wipe out the very names of idols, so they are forgotten, and remove false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

f.w: cut off the names of the idols

n: False prophecy will be so detested that even a false prophet’s own parents will condemn him, as the law of Moses required.

f.w: thou speakest lies in the name of the LORD

n: False prophets will be ashamed of their visions and stop wearing the hairy cloak prophets wore, which they used to deceive.

f.g: A hairy mantle, like Elijah’s (2 Kings 1:8).

n: Each will deny being a prophet: “I’m just a farmer; I’ve worked the land since I was young.”

Someone asks, “What are these wounds on your hands?” He answers, “I got them in my friends’ house.” In context about a false prophet, but the D&C uses similar words of Jesus showing His wounds to the Jews at His coming.

f.w: What are these wounds in thine hands?
in the house of my friends
f.g: Among those who should have loved me.

n: “Awake, sword, against my Shepherd, the man who is my companion!” Strike the Shepherd and the sheep scatter. Jesus quoted this the night of His arrest, applying it to Himself and His disciples.

f.w: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered
the man that is my fellow
f.g: My close associate — one who stands beside God, an exalted description.

n: In the land, two-thirds will be cut off and die, but one-third will remain.

God will refine the surviving third like silver and test them like gold. They will call on Him and He will answer: “They are My people,” and they will say, “The Lord is my God.” Trials purify and bind us to God.

f.w: will refine them as silver is refined
